title: Queue backpressure metric misread causing aggressive scale-down during burst - postmortem & action plan
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: On 2026-02-26 we observed a capacity regression in the text-generation-serving tier during a workload burst that lasted ~18 minutes. Tail latency spiked 3x and error rate increased as replicas dropped aggressively despite a growing request backlog. The immediate cause was a misinterpretation of a queue/backpressure metric used by a KEDA scaler combined with an HPA CPU policy mismatch. This ticket is the consolidated postmortem with investigation notes, decisions, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-26 14:03 UTC - First alert from service-level latency SLO; 14:05 - Grafana shows replica count dropping by 60% while queue depth climbs; 14:07 - On-call investigator executed manual scale-up; 14:14 - Error rate subsided as replicas recovered; 14:30 - Incident declared resolved; 2026-02-26 16:00 - Initial blameless notes captured to Slack incident channel
detection: SLO alerting on P99 latency triggered. Existing autoscale alert thresholds alerted on low CPU and low KEDA trigger count which hid the growing queue backlog until latency surfaced.
root_cause: Three contributing misconfigurations and an emergent regression: (1) The KEDA scaler was wired to a Redis-backed queue-length metric that reported the instantaneous queue length sampled at a 1s cadence; the scaler's scalerThreshold used an arithmetic mean aggregation over 30s which masked short spikes and produced noisy low values between bursts. (2) HPA was configured only on pod CPU utilization with a default stabilization window of 5s; CPU didn't rise immediately for IO-bound requests, so HPA allowed scale-down while the queue still had pending work. (3) A recent change (PR #12844) reduced the KEDA pollInterval from 15s -> 5s (intended to improve responsiveness) but without corresponding smoothing, increasing metric volatility and causing rapid scale-down decisions during the inter-burst gaps.
impact: Approximately 18 minutes of degraded performance for customer-facing endpoints; multiple mid-tier customers reported request timeouts and elevated retry traffic. Estimated exposed requests: ~120k; increased cost from retries and margin loss; one enterprise customer opened an incident ticket during the event.
mitigation: On-call manually pinned the deployment replica count to 6, then increased the minimum replicas via the HPA override while we investigated. We rolled back the recent KEDA pollInterval change in a canary, and enabled a temporary scale-up runbook that triggers an emergency autoscale if queue depth surpasses 95th percentile across a 60s window.
action_items: (Owner: Dimitri) Change KEDA scaler aggregation to use 95th percentile over a 60s window for Redis queue-length metric instead of arithmetic mean. Add tests validating percentile semantics.
(Owner: Sangeeta Rao) Increase HPA scale-down stabilization window from 5s to 120s for the problematic serving workload; document rationale in autoscaling runbook.
(Owner: Platform) Implement a composite scaler policy: require both KEDA queue-length > threshold AND HPA CPU > low-threshold for scale-down decisions for IO-heavy pods.
(Owner: Maya) Add an emergency guardrail in the autoscaler controller to refuse scale-down below 'min_replicas_during_burst' when external-backpressure metric is non-zero.
(Owner: Rafael) Add synthetic warmup traffic job that runs during business-critical hours to keep a minimum cohort warm for 30 minutes following detected high-latency events.
(Owner: Observability) Create a new Grafana panel and alert for 'replica decrease while queue depth increasing' anomaly and add automated PagerDuty escalation.
(Owner: Docs) Update public 'Autoscaling Best Practices' guide with a dedicated section about composite metrics and stabilization windows and link to the new runbook.
(Owner: Security) Review the KEDA metric endpoints for exposure and ensure Redis metrics require read-only role tokens (low risk but record to audit).
completed_items: Rolled back KEDA pollInterval change (PR #12890) and monitored in canary for 48 hours - completed 2026-02-27
Emergency HPA override applied during incident - completed 2026-02-26
Created incident Confluence page and attached diagnostic graphs - completed 2026-02-26
next_steps_and_timeline: By 2026-03-05: merge KEDA percentile change and HPA stabilization window updates (target). By 2026-03-10: deploy composite scale policy behind feature flag and run 1-week canary. By 2026-03-20: promote changes to prod after SLA validation and runbook updates. Follow-up retrospective on 2026-03-22.
retrospective_notes: Communications: on-call escalation path worked but the initial alerting surface area was insufficient; add runbook steps to inspect queue metrics first. Instrumentation: metric aggregation semantics matter — we will standardize aggregator choices (mean vs percentile) across all KEDA scalers. Decision trade-offs: tighter poll intervals reduce detection latency but increase volatility; standard solution is shorter poll with percentile smoothing and longer stabilization for scale-down. We agreed to prefer conservative scale-down defaults for bursty IO workloads.
resolution_summary: Root cause was a coupling of noisy, mean-aggregated queue metrics and aggressive scale-down behavior after a recent pollInterval change. We implemented immediate mitigations (rollback and HPA override) and defined a set of durable controls (percentile aggregation, longer scale-down windows, composite scale policy, warmup job, and alerting) to prevent recurrence.
